To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the effect of data parallalism is characterized by the scaling trend, and (2) the effect of sparsity is characterized by the difficulty of training.
(i) the number of training steps required to converge is proportional to the batch size, and (ii) the effect of data sparsity is proportional to the smoothness of the objective function.
(a) the number of training steps required for convergence increases linearly with batch size, and (b) the number of steps increases exponentially with sparsity.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effects of data and model parallelism on neural network training; we conduct extensive experiments on various workloads, and further, develop a theoretical analysis to explain our observations, which provides a better account of data and model parallism on neural network optimization.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the difficulty of training under both data parallelism and under sparsity is proportional to the product of batch size and number pruning, and the difficulty of training is also proportional to the number of parameters in the neural network model.

data parallelism can be used as an effective way to reduce the number of training steps for neural network training, while sparsity can increase the number of training step, which is in line with our experimental observations and theoretical analysis.

, for data parallelism, the effect of increasing batch size is to increase the number of training steps needed to reach the same level of accuracy; and for sparsity, the effect of pruning parameters in a model is to increase the difficulty of training, measured by the number of training epochs required for convergence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of data-parallelism and sparsity can be well understood by the convergence rate of the underlying optimization algorithm, and the smoothness of the objective landscape.

we have provided a better understanding on neural network training by analyzing the effects of two factors in neural networks: data parallelism, which is the main driving force of training speedup in modern deep learning, and sparsity, which is a promising direction of reducing computational and memory cost.

we provide a better understanding of the effects of two important factors on neural network training, and that the theoretical analysis can serve as a guideline for practitioners to choose appropriate metaparameters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
data parallelism and model sparsity are complementary, and thus, can be used to achieve better performance in neural network training.

data parallelism can be beneficial to training, but the benefits can diminish as the number of training steps increases; and sparsity is detrimental to training, but it can be overcome by data parallelism.
the effects of data and sparsity are not independent of each other, but are coupled in the sense that the effect of one factor is determined by the other factor.
